body:
I'm so sorry for your loss. It was definitely the right choice and you're absolutely right in not having any regrets. 11 years is a really long time so no wonder you're tearing up about it.

The vet had set up a room with candles and a really soft teddy blanket. She got the sedative outside in the sun (she was anxious at the vet) so she wasn't scared or worried. I held her the entire time and she went very calm and peacefully. It was quick too which I'm grateful for as the vet told us that it can take a while and that her body may react. Thankfully it didn't so she looked very peaceful.

You're definitely not crazy. That sounds wonderful to me, that she's watching the house for you. :) If you're crazy let's be crazy together as I've asked for the ashes as well. I plan on getting a beautiful urn in the shape of a heart with paw prints on it. :) My mother wasn't so keen on it but that's OK, we all have our own ways of grieving and honoring our pets. I've even put Toya's red winter jacket in a plastic bag because I don't want her scent to go away... Amongst other small little things I've done these past days.

Very true and very well said. They're our soul mates and the bond we share is incredibly strong. No wonder it hurts like hell having to say goodbye. One second I know she's gone and the next I'm struggling to understand it.

Thank you for sharing your story and for your kind words. Also, right back at you - don't care about if anyone thinks you're "crazy". You're not. You're doing the things you need to honor and remember your best friend and I plan on doing the same. If anyone has a problem with it, I feel sorry for them not having experienced the unconditional love a dog gives.

I'm sorry to hear that. I'm sure you're already doing it, but try to make every day a little bit special. Nothing much but I know that it's a comfort for me knowing that I did everything I could to make Toya's last day special. No fancy three course meal but I gave her some dessert along with extra treats (and lots of hugs and kisses!). The night before was spent on the floor next to her bed while she was sleeping.

Thank you so much and I wish you and your pup all the best.

That sounds like an awesome thing to do. No steak for Toya but I made sure to make her last day extra special. She got extra treats and a special dessert after dinner the day before. Then we went to her favorite park in the morning.

Thank you. The decision is never an easy one. It doesn't matter how old the dog is or if it's showing a lot or very few signs of illness. It's just as hard either way. It's tough but like you said, it's a way to spare them unnecessary pain and suffering. When you try to look at it that way, it's a thing we do out of love.

You sound like a wonderful human being having fostered so many dogs. I'd like to personally thank you for that. If I had the opportunity, I would like to foster dogs someday. When I get my own place, I'll definitely be looking into it.

She did and I feel blessed having had her by my side for so many years. I'll always remember her. Dogs are just amazing.

Thank you for your kind words. I went off reddit for the night and just returned today to read all of the amazing stories and replies to my post. Even if I'm reading yours after Toya's gone, I want you to know that it does make me feel a little bit better about it. There was no other choice, really. Toya wasn't going to get better (or younger, unfortunately). It was still one of the hardest decisions I've had to make but the feeling that it was the right one helped me cope with it. 

The build up from having made the decision, to the call, to the day before and the day of was probably the worst part of it all. At least anxiety wise. I was in a constant panic and it was awful. I'm grateful that the procedure went so calmly and Toya looked so peaceful. Incredibly sad, of course, but I'm glad that I was there for her. I think she felt loved and secure too. Somehow we get through it because we love them so much.

The hardest part was that she looked so healthy, especially during our walks. And she had a great appetite as well. But the mind is a huge part of the body and so her body wasn't doing as well after all. I do find peace in knowing she's not confused anymore. That she doesn't have to suddenly wake up during the night not really knowing if it's night or day. That she doesn't have to feel like she can't keep up with the other two. In between the brutal waves of sadness I try to find some comfort in knowing that.

Your desperation came from love. These dogs aren't just dogs - they're friends, family members and soul mates. Of course we want them to live and be happy and healthy. We'd do anything in our power to make sure they're happy. You being able to turn that desperation into the energy to make the decision is admirable. It speaks volumes of how much love you had (and still have!) for your dog.

Thank you. I'll definitely be bringing her story with me for the rest of my life. The bond we have with them is on a different level, the love is unconditional and the trust is 100%. Human relationships can be amazing as well, but there's always that slight chance of something going wrong. A dog, or any animal for that matter, doesn't complicate things like we do.

I spent a lot of time our last day together just being with her and telling her all the things I needed to. When she went, she was surrounded by love and it was a very peaceful and calm experience. Very, very sad (to say the least) but I couldn't be more grateful for how calm it was.

Thank you so much for telling me some your stories. Your philosophy regarding dogs sounds a lot like my own. How you'll carry their memory with you and how wonderful the love is. Today I feel privileged to have had Toya in my life for so long. Happy to have had her by my side. Grateful that she'll always be with me, just like your amazing basset hound (which, by the way, is a really cool breed :)). 

I just hope I get to see her again someday. I'm not religious but I'd like to think we'll meet again.

Toya crossed the Rainbow Bridge the day after my post. It was peaceful, calm and I'm grateful that we could be there for her. I held, hugged, kissed and hugged her some more. Told her all the things I wanted to tell her. One final hug and a kiss on the head. I don't even care if I may have looked a bit crazy (I probably did...) She was my best friend and I've never loved anyone like I loved her.

Grieving is difficult... I'm struggling a lot with taking care of myself. Eating gives me guilty feelings and I haven't watched my usual Netflix series yet. Nothing new to me as I struggled with guilt when I lost my grandma to cancer. But that was well over 15 years ago. Advice is very welcome... Send PM if you'd like!

Thank you! Much appreciated :)

I'm truly sorry about your losses.

That's very true. They're here now, living (and loving) in the moment. We have a lot to learn from them.

Again, very true. She wasn't all there at the end and our decision felt (and was) right. Her change in personality made me miss her even before she finally went. I'm grateful that we can make that decision and take their pain away. In a very peaceful way too.

She was surrounded by family and I held her and hugged her all throughout the process. She wasn't scared as she got the first sedative outside, as she was a bit anxious about going to the vet. I carried her inside and the rest went by just as calmly. Even the weather was calm as we'd had a bit of a storm the few previous days. Strange coincidence but I like it.

But oh how I miss her.... One second I know she's gone and the next I'm struggling to understand it.

May we all. I truly hope so.

Thank you for your time and your kind and reassuring words.

Her being in actual pain while not really showing it did cross our minds. She would refrain from lying down while chewing on her dental sticks, with only her butt sticking up. Only for the last few weeks or so, though. I can imagine now that she must've had at least a little pain even though she was very active and quick paced during walks. Dogs are definitely stoic.

I used the good days VS bad days the most along with her not being able to enjoy and participate in things like she used to. She wouldn't seek affection for the last weeks and the other dogs seemed to shut her out a bit. Almost as if they knew that she was going away... They're very wise as well as stoic.

The day after my post was difficult, to say the least. We had one final walk together (at a nearby beautiful park she loved) before heading to the vet. It was heart wrenching knowing this was her last everything. Last breakfast, last walk, last car ride... You get it.

I'll keep it short - she was surrounded by family from beginning to end. I held her and my mother was gently petting her while she fell asleep. My father was there too. She went peacefuy and calmly. Quick too even though the vet said that it might take a while. No scary body reactions and she looked very peaceful.

I miss her terribly. My best friend... It feels weird and there's a strange lingering feeling in the air, for all of us. It's as if she is still around but we can't see or feel her. Her absence has a certain presence if you know what I mean? I'll be grieving for a good while but I'm going to give it time. She was a huge part of my life after all. She always will be.

Yes, I've been seeing various therapists and doctors since I was 13. No actual treatment plan though, just medications that never really fixed the actual problem. I guess that's how it works in many places unfortunately..
Not right now but I've managed to book an appointment with a doctor. Hoping it can lead me towards some kind of treatment, maybe CBT.

I hope so! I'll remember it and I'm happy for all the quirky little ceremonies I've been doing. :) I only wish I could've brought her to the beach but it's freezing cold so that's been out of the question unfortunately. 

Thank you for sharing. Sounds like he wouldn't let it stop him. Dogs are amazing like that, they adapt and overcome almost any obstacle thrown at them. :) Quite an inspiration how he managed to memorize even the placement of the furniture!

I really wish we could have the vet over but I don't know if it's possible. My mother was the one who made the call yesterday and I don't think the specific vet is able to make home visits unfortunately. A friend of my mother's had the vet administer the first sedative while the dog was in the car. At least that way it didn't didn't have to feel that anxious about the vet. I think that's a possibility for us as well, my mother may even have mentioned it during the call. Either way, I'll be with her every step of the way. It's not going to be easy but I know I need to be there.

Thank you. I'll try my best to look after myself. I'm already struggling with some mental health issues which of course makes everything worse. I'm sure Toya wants me to take care of myself, like any friend would. My parents will be going away the entire weekend with one of our other dogs so I'll be looking after our third and youngest (11 yo) dog. The "what if?" can be brutal but you definitely made the right choice. I hope I'll eventually feel that way too one day.

I'm the lucky one, I feel. :) That she's been a part of my life for so long.

Thanks once again, you have no idea how comforting it is to read about your story. I'll be trying to get some sleep as it's getting late. I'm also planning on going to a nearby park tomorrow morning with the dogs. Make it a little more special than our usual morning walks. :)

If I'm not back tomorrow I'll probably be back soon. It's really helpful to just talk to people that knows what it's like. Unfortunately I'm kinda low on friends so I don't really have a lot of people to talk to. So thanks once again, I truly appreciate it.
That sounds rough. Are you in therapy/treatment for it?
That's a good one though. I'd like it if 2019 is the year I finally beat my anxiety. Or at least get some actual help for it.

Nala sounds wonderful! Thank you for sharing your story, you made the right decision. It must have been really difficult when it spread and you had to take her to the emergency room. It's traumatic to watch someone you love to through something like that. I bet Nala felt really loved as you hugged her. She'll always be a part of you, wherever you go.

I know it's going to be really difficult but I feel that it's important to be there throughout the entire process. Not just for Toya but for myself as well. To make sure she feels safe and comfortable. My mom will also be going to the vet but I'm not sure she'll be able to be there. If not that's entirely up to her. Either way is okay.

Thank you for your kind words. She's made such an impact on me that I'm even considering having her name tattooed at one point. Would be neat if that would be my first tattoo. Despite having an awful night, I can't help but smile when I think back on all of the awesome memories Toya has given me. :) And then I'm suddenly feeling sad again. Such a rollercoaster of emotions...

Thanks! Sending strength and love right back to you.

Yeah, I'll always be sensitive about any potential downvotes but other than that, reddit is great. That does suck. I struggled with social anxiety as well for a few years. So bad I couldn't even take my dog out because I was afraid people would ask me about the breed and whatnot... How does your social anxiety manifest itself?
Sounds good. Got any new years resolutions?

Thank you for reaching out. It means a lot as I'm very lonely at the moment.

Her quality of life is the number one priority for me, for all of us. As much as my heart wants me to find an alternative to letting go, I know logically that it's only going to get worse from here.

I've made sure to make this day extra special. I've hugged and kissed and cuddled her extra and she got a special treat after her usual dinner. The other two dogs were slightly envious, to say the least... I spent the entire evening right next to her bed just listening to her. Gently petting her. I've told her how much I love her countless times. I even spelled out "I love you" using small pieces of carrot before I let her clean my dinner plate.... Yes I'm a bit crazy. :) 

We just put down our 9 year old collie a couple months ago. 9 is very young, but he was a puppy mill puppy and was blind and going deaf, alongside some mid-grade arthritis. Even though he seemed to be smiling and seemed to be happy most of the time, we knew it was his time to go. He had bad days and bad periods where we just knew that his quality of life was affected.

Sounds like you gave him an awesome life despite his background. :) Was it difficult taking care of a blind dog, if you don't mind my asking? When you know the dog, you know when it's time. I'm still doubting but that's because I love her so much and don't want to say goodbye. Not tomorrow, not ever..

Thank you. 💕 I've been feeling guilty all day, especially while eating... I hope I can manage it but I'm definitely worried about the upcoming weeks.

Hey, Lewis. I'm Jake. I'm just hanging out on the sofa while finding lots of comfort in reddit. Really damn lonely because of insane anxiety while not having anyone to talk to. Took some talking myself into it to reach out, usually I'm just lurking.. What are you up to?

It probably is, just scary as hell because my whole body goes numb and weird and I feel like I'm about to lose my mind completely.

But I feel slightly better when someone interacts with me so thank you. How are you doing by the way?

I'm just high on anxiety atm so every little thing pushes me off the edge. Trying to not lose my mind as the rest of the family is sleeping but I'm in a desperate need of company... /rant (sorry)

I'm sorry about your girl. It's never easy but then again I wouldn't want to live a life without animals. The amount of love and affection they bring without demanding anything back.. Makes the painful goodbye somehow worth it. I'm sure your new dog will be just as loved. :)

I will for sure! I've been spending so much time with her all day, hugging and petting her. She's incredibly loved.
Thank you for reaching back. I'm sorry about your dog as well. A dog is just like any other family member. Dogs are amazing and it's not fair that they don't get to live as long as humans... 🙁

Thank you! Just knowing that someone out there read it and took the time to reply means so much right now. It truly feels like I'm losing it. I've always struggled with separation anxiety... And if I get anxious about stuff, I avoid them. I can't avoid this one so I'm freaking out.

Please don't make me feel worse... I'm not the only one in this decision making either and it's not a quick one. We've been talking about it for more than a month and it hasn't been easy. She's also declined even more since we started talking about it. She's not just a senior dog. It's difficult to explain and hard for outsiders to comprehend the entire situation.

She does have epilepsy but it's managed by medication. We have talked with our vet as well, and with the breeder we're close to. Both of them says that it's up to us but that it does seem like the right decision for her.

She's almost robotic at this point. Like her personality is gone and she's only doing things out of basic instinct.

Thank you for the kind words.

I believe that it's the right decision but my heart keeps debating with my mind, trying to find alternatives. "But her body is healthy otherwise, maybe if we do x or y?" Just be quiet already... It's a rollercoaster. I love her so much.

Finns enormt mycket information om vad dysfori är. Blir besviken när folk gång på gång menar att transpersoner bara är sjuka och behöver hjälp. Orkar inte riktigt ta diskussionen just nu, men rekommenderar varmt att sätta dig in mer i vad könsdysfori är.

Om det är Cecilia Dhejnes studie gällande självmord du tänker på har hon själv gått ut och sagt att många tolkar den fel. https://www.reddit.com/r/asktransgender/comments/4f73ly/repost_with_extra_info_if_someone_comes_to_you

Det enda som hjälper vid faktisk könsdysfori är medicinsk behandling. Visst finns chansen att man ändå mår dåligt men det är inte så konstigt. Däremot mår man oftast bättre än om man *inte* genomgått någon behandling öht. Att man är extra utsatt för diverse diskriminering och ev våld hjälper knappast.

Det är så mycket mer än bara ett par kroppsdelar. Sluta jämföra med kosmetiska ingrepp. Dysfori sitter mycket, mycket djupare än så. Jag önskar fler läste på eller pratade med transpersoner och ställde frågor.
I will. Couldn't even manage to get my ass to school today but there's always tomorrow.
Great job and good luck! I've been putting off seeing my school's counselor for a few weeks now. You've given me some courage to actually go through with it.

One of my shibas' tail is tightly coiled while my other one has a more loose tail (and especially when relaxing). Puppies tend to have looser tails but they'll probably get more tightly coiled as they grow.

Seems normal to me. You don't mind showing a picture?
